conventions.convention: Spacetime is smooth four-dimensional Minkowski space with metric diag(-1,1,1,1); natural units c=ℏ=1 determine engineering dimensions.
The gauge group is the direct product SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1), on the trivial bundle only. Hypercharge is represented by the integer character z^(6Y), with Higgs charge 3.
Right-principal connections use D=∂+ρ*(A) and F=dA+[A∧A]/2. With A=igW, the component non-Abelian field strength has a minus sign in its quadratic gauge-potential term.
The reference radius v>0 need not be a vacuum radius. A vacuum interpretation requires a local minimum of the full retained potential, whose dimension-six Q_H contribution is -C_H s³/Λ_op².
HEFT uses h∈(-v,∞), U∈SU(2), and U↦g_L U diag(z³,z⁻³)^(-1). Its displayed scalar density assumes positive K and F_C on the field range used, K(0)=F_C(0)=1, and V′(0)=0.

The Warsaw contract selects three-family, baryon- and lepton-number-conserving source representatives through dimension six, jet order two, field degree six, and loop order zero. It adopts a coefficient list without locally proving classification or equality of physical and algebraic invariant spaces.

Canonical dimension and the HEFT chiral/loop count are distinct. The latter retains leading order and one-loop counterterm classes while leaving smooth h/v dependence untruncated; neither count supplies numerical remainder bounds.
The polynomial-degree bound concerns the unnormalized radial variable h/v before further scalar reparametrization, and excludes H=0.

The example defines Q_HBox using the local mostly-plus d’Alembertian, assumes vanishing boundary terms, and requires K(0)>0 for its local canonical coordinate. Its inverse-square-root coupling is an exact coefficient calculation in the selected truncated action, with no discarded-order bound.

load_bearing.statement: Adopt the stated smooth three-family Standard Model fields on the trivial direct-product gauge bundle, with exact B- and L-neutrality selection rules for retained formal interactions, dimension-six truncation, and independent coefficient scale Λ_op. The model asserts no functional measure, ultraviolet completion, or empirical realization.
A scalar field is a smooth map h:M→(-v,∞), invariant under the electroweak gauge group, and the Goldstone field is a smooth map U:M→SU(2), with U↦g_L U diag(z³,z⁻³)^(-1).

The Warsaw coefficient contract is the finite dimension-six source list in Tables 2 and 3 of Grzadkowski et al., with exact baryon- and lepton-number conservation: 15 bosonic, 19 single-fermion-current and 25 four-fermion structures before family multiplicities and Hermitian conjugates.

Φ(h,U)=(v+h)Ue₂/√2 is an equivariant smooth diffeomorphism from (-v,∞)×SU(2) onto C²\{0}, with inverse h=√2(H†H)^(1/2)-v and U=(iσ²H*,H)/(H†H)^(1/2). Substitution into the selected finite SMEFT representatives gives polynomial radial coefficients of degree at most six and a finite linear coefficient map f=Rc, before further field reparametrization.

concerns.concern: The Postulate assigns quarks B=1/3 and says that the corresponding U(1)_B transformations multiply fields by the phase determined by their charge, but does not specify the group parameter or its period. With the usual 2π-periodic parameter, exp(iθ/3) is not a well-defined character of U(1). Specify the baryon-circle normalization, for example the integer character charge 3B, or an explicitly defined covering/quotient action. Neutrality selection rules themselves are unaffected. HEFT and the Warsaw contract inherit this unresolved global-action convention.

The graph definition says each vertex has the indicated field half-edges, but m_l and r_s specify only gauge and Goldstone half-edges. The adopted F_C(h) Tr((DU)†DU) sector also generates vertices with gauge, Goldstone and arbitrarily many singlet-h half-edges, including WWh. Clarify explicitly that such singlet decorations are admitted and how they contribute to m and r without an additional subtraction. Otherwise the defined graph class does not clearly cover diagrams of the supplied HEFT model. The displayed degree formula and six structural families agree with [Buchalla–Catà–Krause, §3, equations (10)–(12)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1307.5017).

The title says the selected SMEFT model 'is a restricted HEFT branch', whereas the proved Statement establishes a field substitution and polynomial coefficient map. The adopted HEFT postulate additionally fixes K(0)=F_C(0)=1, positivity on the used range and V′(0)=0; arbitrary selected SMEFT coefficients and reference v need not satisfy these for the total transformed scalar density. The example itself obtains K(0)=1+2C_HBox v²/Λ_op². Explain whether these contributions are allocated to higher interactions or whether 'branch' here denotes only the formal substitution image. The explicit diffeomorphism and polynomial-map proof do not themselves fail.

seams_checked.note: The SMEFT and Warsaw items preserve the physical-operator supplier's finite-cutoff, coefficient-scale and formal-quotient qualifications. No completeness or observable-equivalence theorem is inferred.
This is a page-order prerequisite. No assigned item invokes the matching or scale-independence theorem, or turns its conditional hypotheses into a computed SMEFT coefficient or RG flow.

Right-principal conventions, associated derivatives and Cartan curvature are retained. Substitution of anti-Hermitian ig times Hermitian generators yields the stated minus sign in component field strengths.

The Warsaw contract explicitly treats the algebraic quotient as formal and does not strengthen its selected-relation definition into a complete physical classification. The local-operator supplier is used for engineering dimensions.

The heavy-chiral threshold definition cites HEFT for shared Minkowski spacetime and metric only. Its separate U(1)_V representations, chiral sector and anomaly inputs are specified locally; they are not attributed to the electroweak postulate.

The A-page statistical definitions do not use SMEFT physical premises. The page prerequisite supplies context for its companion's coefficient interpretations, without making mathematical statistics depend on physics.

The three SMEFT reports cite field and Warsaw conventions as formulation prerequisites. Their selected coefficient directions, source-specific truncations and statistical qualifications remain explicit; they do not claim to test the entire coefficient space or prove the postulate.
